key_insight: A variational physics-informed graph neural network (PI-GNN) shifts heterogeneity handling from the neural trial field to the mesh/graph discretization, enabling penalty-free, label-free interface modeling for heterogeneous solids.
engineering_relevance: It offers a consistent surrogate framework for heterogeneous elasticity and hyperelasticity with strong accuracy across large stiffness contrasts, making it useful for parametric studies and inverse material identification.
method: Uses a conforming adaptive mesh graph with constitutive properties assigned per element.
Minimizes the discrete total potential energy as a single unweighted objective with only first derivatives.
Enforces Dirichlet boundary conditions by construction, avoiding interface penalties and transition-width tuning.
evidence_signal: Across stiffness contrasts from 10^-2 to 10^2, the PI-GNN kept von Mises error below 3.58%, while a strong-form PINN reached 5.58% and displacement error dropped to 0.49% versus 7.66% for the PINN.
watch_item: Training is more expensive than a single finite element solve, so the approach is better suited to surrogate modeling and inverse analysis than to replacing one-off FE simulations.
paper_title: A variational physics-informed graph neural network for heterogeneous solid mechanics
